title: Implement A/B Testing and Model Versioning for Inference Services
description: The BizPulse HexaML Inference Suite currently serves the latest production model for all inference requests. The MLOps team wants to introduce a more sophisticated deployment strategy to safely roll out new models. This involves two key features: 1) The ability for a client to request a specific, named model version (e.g., for debugging or targeted rollouts). 2) An automated A/B testing mechanism where a configurable percentage of traffic is routed to a new 'challenger' model, while the rest is served by the 'champion' (production) model. This task requires modifying the API, core domain logic, and infrastructure adapters to support this new functionality over several development sessions.

project_spec.name: BizPulse HexaML Inference Suite
project_spec.description:
BizPulse is a high-performance, C-based machine-learning inference suite that empowers midsize enterprises to embed real-time predictive intelligence directly into their line-of-business workflows (pricing, risk scoring, inventory optimization, churn prevention).  The solution is designed around a strict hexagonal architecture: business-core ports define invariant concepts such as Forecast, PricingRule, CustomerRisk, while adapters on the outside handle model serving, feature ingestion, visualization dashboards and automated retraining triggers coming from data-ops events.

The project orchestrates the full MLOps lifecycle in production—data_preprocessing and feature_engineering pipelines transform raw operational data feeds into reusable feature vectors that are persisted in a pluggable Feature Store.  An internal Model Registry coordinates hyperparameter_tuning experiments executed by GPU-backed workers; experiment_tracking metadata is versioned and exposed through a thin REST adapter.  Deployed models are exposed via low-latency gRPC endpoints; model_evaluation reports are pushed to a monitoring bus that drives automated_retraining when drift is detected.  Business analysts can immediately consume data_visualization artifacts through a web UI without coupling to the core inference logic, maintaining the purity of the domain layer.

By applying Pipeline_Pattern stages inside each adapter and leveraging Factory_Pattern + Strategy_Pattern for model selection at runtime, BizPulse stays fully configurable while meeting stringent enterprise governance requirements.
dependencies: ONNX Runtime C API (high-performance model inference)
Prometheus C client (runtime metrics for MLOps_Architecture)
